title: Valuative domination criterion for eta-normal flat schemes
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K$. Let $C,X,Y$ be reduced schemes flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite type over $S$, and let $a:X\to C$ and $b:Y\to C$ be $\eta$-modifications. Suppose $Y$ is $\eta$-normal, meaning every finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] $\eta$-modification of $Y$ is an isomorphism. For every finite-height valuation ring $V\subseteq K$ with fraction field $K$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to S$ agreeing with the generic map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, assume there exists a morphism $h_V:Y_V\to X_V$ over $C_V$, where subscript $V$ denotes base change [def-pc-fibre-product] to $\operatorname{Spec}V$. Then there exists an $S$-morphism $h:Y\to X$ with $ah=b$, whose generic fibre is $a_\eta^{-1}b_\eta$. Here reduced means local rings have no nonzero nilpotents; valuation ring means that for each $u\in K^\times$ at least one of $u,u^{-1}$ lies in $V$, and finite height means its prime ideals form a finite chain. An $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism inducing an isomorphism on the generic fibre and between schematically dense open subschemes; an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.
